Cristiano Ronaldo has been voted the greatest European striker of the 21st century, finishing ahead of French football legend Thierry Henry and England captain Harry Kane in a public poll conducted by BBC Sport on Thursday. Tens of thousands of football fans took part in the voting, selecting their favourites from a 20-man shortlist drawn up by a panel of experts. The results were subsequently discussed by European football experts Guillem Balague, Julien Laurens and Raphael Honigstein on the Euro Leagues podcast. Ronaldo claimed the top position following an extraordinary career that has seen him establish himself as one of football’s most prolific goalscorers. The Portuguese superstar has represented Sporting Lisbon, Manchester United, Real Madrid, Juventus and Al-Nassr, winning major honours and setting remarkable scoring records along the way. Discussing Ronaldo’s achievement, Balague described him as the best striker in history, highlighting his incredible statistics, ambition and determination to reach the 1,000-goal milestone. Laurens also praised the forward’s natural goalscoring instinct and exceptional work ethic, predicting that his achievements may never be matched. Thierry Henry finished second, making him the highest-ranked retired player on the list. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Henry scored 228 goals for Arsenal and became one of the Premier League’s most celebrated forwards through his combination of pace, elegance, creativity and clinical finishing. England captain Harry Kane completed the top three, following his remarkable goalscoring achievements with Tottenham Hotspur and Bayern Munich. The former Tottenham striker was praised for his intelligence, technical ability, work rate and all-round contribution to his teams.
